description: Natural chamber formed in the bedrock on a sandstone ridge. Excavations revealed a ledge and hearth, with postholes at the front of the chamber suggesting a door was in place. Interpretation as both Roman and a shrine relies on the interpretation of a figure carved into the wall as the god Cocidius.
bibliography: Charlton, and Mitcheson. “Yardhope. A Shrine to Cocidius?” Britannia 14 (1983).
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Yardhope (Northumberland).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
